content.value: , it solved a real problem: getting Dust agents into the browser where most work actually happens. Select text, share a page, start a conversation, all without leaving your tab.

It was a start. But the extension and the web app still felt like two different products. If you tried both, you noticed. The extension was faster to reach but limited in what it could do once you got there.
Full parity with the web app
now does everything the web app does.
: bold, italic, lists, emoji. Your draft auto-saves when you close the sidebar. Conversations display
, reactions, and attached or generated files. You can attach agents, tools, skills, or knowledge sources to any conversation, directly from the sidebar.
Your conversation list and inbox are there too, with unread indicators.
The extension always had access to your current page. What's changed is how agents use that access.
When an agent needs the content of the page you're on, it detects what's there and asks for permission. No manual copy-paste, no "attach page" button. It works across
. And it goes beyond reading: agents can now

The extension also suggests actions based on what it sees. A form on the page? It offers to fill it. Several tabs open? It offers to work across them. You don't need to initiate these workflows; the agent does.
Since the rebuild runs on the same architecture as the web app,
. Gmail, Notion, your CRM, everything, accessible from the extension without switching tabs.
This is the part the web app can't replicate. An agent that reads your browser context, acts on the page, and calls your connected tools, all from a sidebar that's one keyboard shortcut away.
, in addition to Chrome. Same Chrome Web Store install.
Already have the extension? Update from the Chrome Web Store. New to Dust?
